blocks.text: The module documentation defines the router/emitter/manager relationships, ownership privacy rule, fixed error policy, and lifecycle behavior for start, disconnect, user messages, cancel, and resume.
blocks.title: Handler contract

blocks.anchor: HOOK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10.0            # one hook may take this long; then it is cancelled
blocks.text: Constants bound hook, queue, cancellation, and purge behavior. map_error converts known run-family exceptions to fixed protocol codes and sanitized details.
blocks.title: Constants and error mapping

blocks.text: _thread runs synchronous collaborators in a threadpool but waits for a cancelled call to finish. _Turns and _Resume hold per-run queue and resume-rollback state.
blocks.title: Cancellation-safe blocking calls

blocks.text: RunHandlers validates injected limits, caches stable handler identities, exposes defaults, installs one turn runner, deduplicates hooks, and invokes hooks with timeout and type-only logging.
blocks.title: Configuration and hooks

blocks.anchor: async def owned_run(self, conn, msg: dict, *, open_only: bool = True):
blocks.text: The ownership guard hides missing, foreign, malformed, and terminal runs behind run_not_found. Start and user-message handlers create runs or enqueue bounded per-run work, while workers re-read state before each turn.
blocks.title: Ownership and turn dispatch

blocks.anchor: async def on_cancel_request(self, conn, msg: dict) -> None:
blocks.text: Cancellation runs hooks and stops turns before taking the emitter lock, moving the run terminal, and announcing the final state. Missing-buffer endings are handled without an announcement and cleanup retries are scheduled.
blocks.title: Cancellation and cleanup

blocks.text: Disconnect cleanup skips superseded connections. Otherwise it binds each slot-holding run, stops turns, runs disconnect hooks, pauses the run, stores a pause event, and unbinds it.
blocks.title: Disconnect pause

blocks.anchor: async def on_run_resume(self, conn, msg: dict) -> None:
blocks.text: Resume binds and locks the run, delegates buffer attachment and state transition to run_manager, restores emitter sequence, replays missed events, announces running when appropriate, and undoes partial progress on failure.
blocks.title: Resume replay and rollback

blocks.text: install registers the four message handlers and disconnect listener idempotently, and installs the process-wide router as the socket handler when using defaults.
blocks.title: Router installation

gotchas: Synchronous operations are not interrupted when the handler is cancelled.
Ownership failures intentionally hide whether a run exists.
Turn queues are process-local and waiting messages are dropped on stop.

purpose: RunHandlers is the glue between validated socket messages and synchronous run/buffer operations. It enforces ownership, maps internal failures to fixed protocol errors, serializes turns per run, runs bounded hooks, and installs the process-wide router handlers.
summary: Integrates run routing, event emission, lifecycle management, turn queues, cancellation, disconnect, and resume.
